title: Coastal opportunities, local costs
changes: Civilizations assess actual shore towns, ocean paths and available settlement sites before investing in a Boat yard or favoring Navigation. Existing research and paid construction continue independently.

Coastal departures protect current supplies, home workers and household needs. Global first-coast bonuses no longer override ordinary town limits; a useful local prospect does not guarantee a later settlement or era change.

title: Compare the real cost of a reform
changes: Civilizations compare a government change with keeping their current arrangement, including actual reform prices, transition losses, paid work and household needs. The same accounting applies to empty and occupied policy slots.

Income from existing work can fund later costs only after it is earned. Accepted promises and finite local resources stay protected; choices with unresolved dependencies are left unquoted rather than treated as free gains.

title: Make room for working places
changes: Site symbols and short labels make room for the actual buildings and worked land. Visible inspection targets keep their exact town and site identity; crowded views retain the existing Work inspector.
Recorded Survival reasons now distinguish current Food risk from rebuilding the existing safety buffer. Paid production, construction, geography and autonomous choice weights are unchanged.
